title: Apocalypse Bringer Mynoghra
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Takuto Ira dies young of illness and wakes inside his favorite strategy game as ruler of Mynoghra, a civilization the game classes as evil, with his monstrous retainer Atou. He wants only to build a peaceful settlement in the forest, but refugee races fleeing human racism seek his protection, and human kingdoms treat Mynoghra as a threat.
life_message: Goodness is shown in protecting the outcast and building a home for them, whatever label the world puts on you.

content.note: Atou kills invading knights; heart-eating for power (Wikipedia, characters may run past manga); AniList Gore and Cannibalism tags (spoiler, low rank); MU Blood and Gore.
Monstrous allies, war with a Holy Kingdom and a Demon Lord's generals (Wikipedia); AniList Tragedy tag.
Takuto and Atou's mutual crush (Wikipedia); AniList Nudity (spoiler, rank 20); MU Big Breasts (2 votes); MangaDex suggestive.
Takuto's terminal illness and death before rebirth (Yen Press blurb, MU Illness).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Takuto will defend his home if attacked (Wikipedia); invading knights are killed rather than tried.

Order vs freedom.evidence: A ruler with psychic command over subordinates builds an ordered settlement.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Found family: Isla as adoptive mother, loyal retainers, sheltered races.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: King of Ruin with Eight Heroes and devoted attendants (Wikipedia).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Game-logic and strategy framing; religious kingdom portrayed as hostile.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Food, territory and defense dominate (MU Kingdom Building, Territory Management).

folkways.japan: Devoted retainers serving a lord and the isekai game-world frame are common in Japanese web-novel fiction.

delivery.evidence: ANN anime preview: Takuto and Atou's goodness drives the story and the 'evil' label is relative; no reviewer calls it preachy.

personified.ideology: goodness under a label the world calls evil

delivery.note: The idea that labels do not decide goodness is clear in the setup; how fairly the human kingdoms are drawn is not yet established (to verify).

winners_losers: The outcast 'evil' civilization and its refugees gain sympathy; the self-righteous Holy Kingdom and racist human states lose it.
